items.title: Propagate the KI-1 prior-art finding into README and REPORT
items.acceptance: README's differentiation claim and REPORT's KI-1 row both state the completed prior-art finding verbatim from SPEC.md (nearest npm package lunarphase-js v2.0.3 is a naive mean-synodic modulo with zero periodic corrections and emoji-only 'hemisphere support', not a CLI; astronomia v4.2.0 is a genuine Meeus port deliberately not adopted as a dependency) in place of the old 'never swept / permission-blocked' language.
items.notes:
PLAN grep (conductor-verified): zero hits for lunarphase-js|astronomia|prior-art in README.md; REPORT.md's KI-1 row still reads 'never swept... permission-blocked', which is now stale. The finding is written out in SPEC.md 'Domain rules' - copy it, do not re-derive it. L-026: never hand-edit captured output.

ATTEMPT 1 FAILED THE GATE (cycle 2), reverted. Model escalated haiku->sonnet. Two defects, both must be avoided on the retry:
(1) GATE-FAILER - FABRICATED MAGNITUDE. The README note asserted the naive modulo gives '4-hour phase errors'. Conductor-verified: the string '4-hour' appears NOWHERE in the repo except the line the builder wrote - not in SPEC.md, not in src/astro.js, not in any prior doc. SPEC's prior-art bullet states 'zero periodic correction terms' and never quantifies the error. It is also probably wrong in the understating direction (Meeus ch.49's single largest periodic term for new/full moon is ~0.40720 d ~= 9.8 h, and the terms sum), so it silently WEAKENS our own differentiation claim while being unverifiable. RULE FOR THE RETRY: state the structural fact (zero periodic corrections vs a full Meeus series) and do NOT quantify the error at all unless the number is computed in-repo and shown.
(2) SHOULD-FIX - the retry put the string 'closed' in the REPORT.md Known Issues table's SEVERITY column, whose other values are medium/low. That conflates status with severity and drops KI-1's real severity (state.json: low). Keep severity a severity; if a resolved-status convention is needed, T-108 owns the table reconciliation - coordinate, do not invent a convention unilaterally here.
CONDUCTOR RULING: this escalation to sonnet must SURVIVE the gear-1 docs demotion rule (which would otherwise push docs items sonnet->haiku). The failure mode was fabrication under the cheaper tier; demoting it back would just reproduce the defect.

ATTEMPT 2 PASSED THE GATE (cycle 4) at sonnet; seven conductor-run checks, evidence in .swarm/runs/cycle-004-verify-T-101.txt. Zero magnitudes introduced (verified by extracting every numeric token from the added lines: only 'KI-1', a list ordinal, and the two SPEC-verbatim version strings v2.0.3/v4.2.0). Severity column holds only severities; KI-1's cell corrected medium->low to match state.json. Stale never-swept language gone from BOTH the table row and the hand-off section. 104/104 green. KI-1 resolved.

CORRECTION TO THE CYCLE-2 RECORD: the stated reason above - that '4-hour' appears NOWHERE in the repo - was a too-narrow grep for the hyphenated literal. The figure IS in-repo in words at README.md:156-157, REPORT.md:34 and test/astro.test.js:96. The gate DECISION was still right: it is a single hand-computed datapoint for the 2000-01-06 lunation, and attempt 1 lifted it into a general per-package error claim about a package nobody ran (understating besides - the largest single ch.49 term is ~9.8h and the terms sum). The retry brief carried this correction so the builder would not be licensed by its own grep.

items.title: Fix KI-6: nextFullMoon throws instead of returning an out-of-range Invalid Date
items.acceptance: Calling nextFullMoon() with a valid Date whose resulting full-moon instant falls outside the representable JS Date range throws a TypeError, matching the module's existing throw-on-bad-input behaviour, instead of silently returning an Invalid Date that later surfaces as an uncaught RangeError from --json's toISOString().
items.notes:
CONDUCTOR-REPRODUCED at cycle 1, first-hand:
  nextFullMoon(new Date(8.64e15)) -> Invalid Date   (silent)
  .toISOString()                  -> RangeError: Invalid time value
  nextFullMoon('not a date')      -> TypeError: nextFullMoon expects a valid Date
PLAN grep (conductor-verified): test/astro.test.js has no hits for RangeError|8640000000000000|275760; its two nextFullMoon throw-tests cover bad INPUT only, never the out-of-range OUTPUT path. Do NOT touch the Meeus math - this is a guard clause on the return value.

GATE PASS at cycle 3 (six conductor-run checks; evidence in .swarm/runs/cycle-003-verify-T-102.txt). Guard is 4 lines on the return value; Meeus math byte-identical. 102 -> 104 tests green. Non-vacuity confirmed: against `git show HEAD:src/astro.js` the defect-pinning test FAILS, so it closes a real surface. KI-6 resolved.

items.title: Declare the KI-7 supported date domain in src/astro.js and pin it with a SAMPLED consistency test
items.acceptance: src/astro.js exports a named constant declaring an explicit supported date-range domain for phaseName/illumination consistency, with a doc comment stating WHY the two Meeus series (ch.48 elongation vs ch.49 instant tables) are only guaranteed consistent inside it. test/astro.test.js SAMPLES points across that declared domain (sampling, never an exhaustive sweep) and asserts the phase name band-discriminator holds at every sampled point.
items.notes:
SPLIT FROM T-103 at cycle 6 (see state.json decisions). This slice owns the MODULE + TEST; the README sentence is T-103b, which deps on this one so the quantity enters the docs only after the repo computes it (standing docs frame rule, cycles 2/4).

CONDUCTOR-MEASURED at cycle 1 - use this, it is sharper than the KI-7 text. The right invariant is a DISCRIMINATOR (L-024): the phase name's illumination BAND must contain the reported illumination - crescent < 0.5, gibbous > 0.5, new < 0.10, full > 0.90 (quarters straddle, exempt). Observed contradictions outside the domain:
  new Date(4.0e15)  -> 'waning gibbous'  ill=0.0385   (gibbous but 3.85% lit)
  new Date(-8.0e15) -> 'waning crescent' ill=0.8053   (crescent but 80.5% lit)
Measured clean region: 0 violations in 32,004 sampled states from year -2000 to 6000; first violation ~72,500 years from 1970. Recommend declaring year 1000-3000 as the supported domain - comfortably inside the measured-clean region with margin. SAMPLED, not exhaustive (taste judge, scope-fits-night).

SCOPE FENCE: this item does NOT change any astronomy. No edits to truePhaseJD, elongationDeg, lunationK, the correction tables, or any polynomial. Adding a constant plus a doc comment plus a test is the whole job. The core is verified against Meeus 49.a/49.b and the SPEC non-goal forbids rewriting it.

The DISCRIMINATOR is the point (L-024): assert the phase name band CONTAINS the reported illumination, not that illumination equals a remembered value. Bands: new < 0.10, waxing/waning crescent < 0.5, waxing/waning gibbous > 0.5, full > 0.90; first/last quarter STRADDLE and are exempt.
items.evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-006-verify-T-103a.txt — astronomy byte-identical to HEAD; 106/106 green; 3733/4000 samples assert (all four bands exercised); conductor mutation (widen endMs to year 80000) turns it RED with a diagnosable message, proving it reads the exported constant AND detects real contradictions; independent re-sample at N=9973 and N=50021 on a jittered off-lattice finds 0 violations.

items.title: State the declared KI-7 supported date domain in README, sourced to the shipping test
items.acceptance: README.md states the same supported date domain that src/astro.js declares, names the consequence of leaving it (phaseName and illumination may contradict each other), and attributes the bound to the in-repo sampled test rather than to an unsourced claim. The domain figures must match the module constant exactly.
items.notes:
SPLIT FROM T-103 at cycle 6. Runs AFTER T-103a so the domain is machine-checked before the README asserts it. STANDING DOCS FRAME RULE (cycles 2 and 4): a quantity may appear only in the frame in which the repo already computes it. Here the frame is exactly what T-103a s test samples - a sampled-clean domain - and the README must not widen it into a proof of correctness outside the sample or into a general accuracy claim.

ATTEMPT 1 FAILED THE GATE at cycle 7 (haiku). Reverted with `git checkout -- README.md`; tree returned clean, 106/106 still green. Read this before retrying - the retry brief is written WITH the correction in it so attempt 2 does not re-argue a settled point.

WHAT ATTEMPT 1 GOT RIGHT (keep all of it): scope fence held (README.md only); the domain figures 1000/3000 were copied correctly from src/astro.js:72-73; NO invented magnitudes (every numeral in the added text already existed in HEAD README or src/astro.js); the consequence was named concretely ('phaseName and illumination may contradict each other') rather than hand-waved; 'Outside this domain, behavior is unspecified' is exactly right; the voice matched the surrounding section.

WHY IT FAILED - ONE CLAUSE. It wrote: 'Over years **1000-3000**, `phaseName` and `illumination` are mutually consistent -- confirmed by test/astro.test.js.' The word CONFIRMED, with no sampling hedge anywhere in the added text, states as established a property the repo only sampled. Every other layer of the repo hedges: src/astro.js says 'SAMPLED-clean, not proven ... not a derived error bound'; test/astro.test.js:386 says 'This SAMPLES -- never exhaustively sweeps --'; the test's own name ends in '(sampled)'. The added README sentence was the ONLY place in the repo asserting the consistency unhedged. Measured at the gate: the test checks 4000 points across a 730,485-day domain = one point per ~183 days, 0.548% of the domain's distinct days. 'Confirmed' asserts a property of a continuum from that sample.

THIS IS NOT A STYLE NOTE. Discriminator the gate applied: if the implementation were wrong at some unsampled instant inside 1000-3000, the module doc comment would still be TRUE ('found no contradiction anywhere in the sample') and the README sentence would be FALSE. A docs item whose job is to document a bound must not make a strictly stronger claim than the module it documents.

WHAT ATTEMPT 2 MUST DO: keep the sentence essentially as-is and carry the hedge into it. The bound is what an in-repo test SAMPLED and found no contradiction in - not what it confirmed, proved, guaranteed, validated or verified. Do not pad the paragraph to compensate; this is a one-clause repair, and the gate will re-check scope, figures and magnitudes exactly as before.

RESIDUAL, NOT A DEFECT IN THIS ITEM (do not 'fix' it, do not widen scope to it): the module's own doc comment glosses the half-open interval [Date.UTC(1000,0,1), Date.UTC(3000,0,1)) as 'calendar years 1000 through 3000', so year 3000 itself is outside the domain but reads as inside. Attempt 1 inherited that phrasing verbatim from the module and was NOT failed for it - matching the module constant is this item's acceptance. Logged separately as T-110.

items.title: Pin KI-5 with a test that measures the documented disc glyph widths
items.acceptance: A test inspects the exact glyph set renderLine/renderBlock draw for the disc across a representative sweep of phases and confirms it matches the documented East Asian Width partition (U+2591, U+2590 Neutral; U+2592, U+2593, U+2588, U+258C, U+258F, U+2595 Ambiguous), so a future glyph change fails the gate instead of drifting silently from the documented widths.
items.notes:
PLAN grep (conductor-verified): zero hits for east asian|Ambiguous|2591|2592|258C across test/. KI-5's measured widths exist ONLY as prose in README/REPORT. This item PINS the defect; it does NOT fix it - the glyph-set redesign stays deferred by budget decision.

GATE PASS cycle 5. Conductor-authored gate (.swarm/runs/verify-gate-T-104.mjs, written at verification time): independent conductor-side derivation of the disc glyph set reproduced the builder's 10 codepoints EXACTLY, and the pin FAILS under all three glyph mutations (add an undocumented Block Element, drop a documented one, change the round limb) - so it is a real pin, not a tautology. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-005-verify-T-104.txt

items.title: Test package-manifest integrity: bin path, main field, zero deps, files list
items.acceptance: A test confirms package.json's bin.moon path resolves to the same file the CLI suites spawn, its main field resolves to an existing module, it declares no dependencies and no devDependencies, and its files allowlist matches what the package actually ships.
items.notes: PLAN grep (conductor-verified): zero hits for package.json|require.resolve|dependencies across test/. REPORT.md lists 'zero runtime dependencies' as a VERIFIED claim that no test has ever checked. NOTE: this item READS package.json but must not MODIFY it - manifests are excluded from builder write scope.

items.title: Test the next-full-moon date label's year-boundary branch
items.acceptance: A test drives the CLI with a clock positioned so the next full moon falls in a later calendar year than the current date and confirms the printed date includes that year; a same-year case confirms the year suffix stays omitted.
items.notes: PLAN grep (conductor-verified): getFullYear appears exactly once in the repo, at bin/moon.js:61 - the ternary that appends or omits the year. No test references it in either direction; the one date-formatting regression pins day-padding at a fixed 2026-01-01 clock that never crosses a year boundary.

items.title: Test that successful CLI invocations write nothing to stderr
items.acceptance: A test confirms every successful invocation mode (default, --compact, --block, --json, --help) produces empty stderr, closing the gap between REPORT.md's 'nothing on stderr on success' VERIFIED claim and a suite that never captures stderr on a passing run.
items.notes: PLAN grep (conductor-verified): 'stderr' appears in test/ only inside the single --bogus exit-2 test (cli.test.js:107-112). L-010: capture the exit status directly, never through a pipe - use spawnSync and read .status/.stderr, do not shell-pipe.

items.title: Reconcile REPORT.md's Known Issues and hand-off with this run's fixes
items.acceptance: REPORT.md's Known Issues table and hand-off section state the resolved/bounded status of KI-1, KI-6 and KI-7 and the newly machine-checked status of KI-5, with no remaining claim that any of them is still open, unswept, or documented in prose only.
items.notes:
Not a test item. Runs LAST by deps - once T-101..T-104 land, REPORT's current statements become false, which is the exact doc-truth failure mode SPEC must-have 6 and L-026 warn about. Also record KI-3 as resolved (remote + gh auth verified at kickoff).

HANDOFF FROM T-101 (cycle 4), three things this item now owns:
(1) RESOLVED-STATUS CONVENTION. KI-1 and KI-6 are both in state.json resolved_issues, but REPORT.md's Known Issues table still LISTS them as rows (KI-1's row now carries the completed finding at severity low; KI-6's row still reads as open). T-101 was explicitly forbidden from inventing a convention in the severity column - that column must stay severities only. THIS item decides the convention (a separate status column, a struck row, a Resolved section - conductor's call) and applies it to KI-1, KI-3, KI-6, and KI-7 once bounded. Do NOT put status strings in the severity column.
(2) The table header still says 'Known issues (7)'. If rows move out, the count moves with them.
(3) RESIDUAL flagged by the T-101 gate, not fixed there because it was outside that item's acceptance: README.md line ~27 opens 'Most terminal moon phase tools compute the phase with a naive synodic-month modulo, which drifts by hours to days.' The sweep substantiates that for ONE package (the nearest), not for 'most', and 'hours to days' is an unsourced pre-existing magnitude. The standing no-unsourced-numbers rule says a quantity may appear only in the frame the repo already computes it in. Either source it, scope it to the one package the sweep actually examined, or drop the magnitude.

items.title: README's KI-5 glyph list omits the round-limb glyphs it actually draws
items.acceptance: README.md's 'Known limitation: terminal glyph width' section accounts for U+25D6 and U+25D7, the round-limb glyphs the disc actually draws for a fully-lit outer cell - either by adding them to the width partition with their correct East Asian Width class, or by explicitly scoping the section's claim to the Block Element shade ramp. No unsourced magnitude may be introduced (standing docs frame rule, cycle 2/4).
items.notes:
FOUND BY THE T-104 BUILD, cycle 5, and independently CONDUCTOR-CONFIRMED by the gate: the disc's observed glyph alphabet is 10 codepoints - the 8 Block Elements the README lists, PLUS U+25D6 and U+25D7 (ROUND_LIMB in src/render.js, drawn for a fully-lit outer cell). The README's width caveat names only the 8. The builder correctly refused to widen the documented table to make its test pass and pinned the two separately in UNDOCUMENTED_DISC_GLYPHS instead, so the test tells the truth about what is and is not covered; this item closes the doc side.
OPEN QUESTION for whoever takes it: this run has NOT established the EAW class of U+25D6/U+25D7 (both are in fact Ambiguous per Unicode, but that is not machine-checked here and must not be asserted from memory - no EAW table may ship, the zero-dep non-goal forbids it). Scoping the section's claim to the Block Element ramp is the honest S-effort option; classifying the two glyphs requires a source. Do not state a class this repo cannot check.

items.title: The KI-7 domain doc comment glosses a half-open interval as an inclusive year range
items.acceptance: src/astro.js's PHASE_ILLUMINATION_CONSISTENCY_DOMAIN doc comment describes the domain in a way consistent with the half-open interval the constant actually defines: endMs is Date.UTC(3000,0,1) EXCLUSIVE, so calendar year 3000 is not in the domain. Comment only - the constant's values must not change, and no test may be weakened or retargeted.
items.notes:
FOUND BY THE T-103b GATE at cycle 7, in the module rather than in the item under test. The comment reads 'calendar years 1000 through 3000 (i.e. [Date.UTC(1000,0,1), Date.UTC(3000,0,1)))'. The bracket notation is correct and self-documenting; the prose gloss before it is off by one calendar year at the top end. Low value - the interval notation sits immediately beside the gloss, so a careful reader is not actually misled - but it propagates: T-103b is required to match the module, so the module's imprecision would be copied into README by construction. Fix the module and the README inherits the correct frame.
DELIBERATELY NOT bundled into T-103b: that item's acceptance is 'the domain figures must match the module constant exactly', and letting a docs builder silently re-scope the module's own claim is the opposite of the discipline this run is enforcing.
